# The Molecule Price Gap

A molecule-level ledger of US vs Canadian drug prices, built from open data.
Independent open-source project by Richardson Dackam. Not affiliated with the
US Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, the Patented Medicine Prices
Review Board, or any government. MIT licensed.

## Question it answers

What does one molecule cost in the US vs Canada?

## Data

- US side: CMS Medicare Part D Spending by Drug, 2024 release (3,625 unique
  drugs in the Overall rows). US amounts are gross of confidential manufacturer
  rebates, so they overstate net US prices by an unknown share. Every price
  comparison in this project carries that caveat.
- Canadian side: Ontario Drug Benefit e-formulary, lowest Drug Benefit Price
  per unit across matched formulary rows (the price Ontario's public plan
  pays pharmacies), converted to USD at the 2024 Bank of Canada average rate.
  PMPRB publishes no machine-readable molecule-level price file, which is
  why the formulary is the Canadian source.
- Identity: generic names normalized to molecules, resolved to RxNorm
  ingredient RxCUI, ATC codes from RxNorm properties.
- Build scripts in scripts/. Raw CMS CSV is not committed; the pipeline
  downloads it from data.cms.gov and caches RxNorm results in
  data/rxnorm_cache.json.

## Use it

- Web: explorer (search by molecule, brand, ATC), findings, charts.
- REST: /api/v1/summary, /api/v1/molecules/search?q=, /api/v1/molecules/{key},
  /api/v1/gaps/ranking, /api/v1/atc. Spec at /api/openapi.json.
- MCP (POST /mcp, streamable HTTP): molecule_lookup, price_gap_ranking,
  atc_breakdown.
- CSV: /data/molecule-ledger.csv

## Rules the build follows

- No em dashes anywhere. No unnecessary semicolons in copy.
- Every sentence carries a number, a mechanism, or a reason.
- Never write "not demos" / "not a demo". Never declare a mission "for good".
